tool_input.command: git diff HEAD -- modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/streaming.go modules/caddyhttp/server.go | head -700; git status --short | head -30

structured_output.summary: I found no unmet criterion and no weakened test. My probe for the per-upstream registry and Caddyfile parsing passed. I did not write separate probes for the integration criteria (reloads, h2, encode/intercept, access logging). They are covered by the task's own tests, which I read but did not re-run. Two small advisories.

findings.text: No test covers detached streams to dynamic upstreams, which are keyed by an empty string and so never closed on upstream removal. The doc comment states this limit, but the behaviour has no test.
gracefulClose calls markResult(reload) even on the detached close path, where closeUpstream has already marked the result; it is harmless because the first mark wins, but it reads as redundant.

coverage.note: Echoes on the stream after two reloads and then closes it gracefully; no separate probe written, relies on this integration test.
The removed stream is closed and the retained one keeps echoing. My probe checks the registry closes only the removed upstream's streams.
Covers both the no-delay and 3s-delay cases, including the stream still echoing during the delay; no separate probe written.
Counts 101 entries in the access log for the default and skip_handshake configs; no separate probe written.
Checks logger name, level (default DEBUG, not logged at INFO), upstream and byte counts; no separate probe written.

After hijack, Write, ReadFrom, Flush and WriteResponse return ErrHijacked and only the raw bytes follow the 101. The encode writer's Hijack guard has no direct unit test; it is exercised through the integration test.
Echo works through encode and intercept for both an echo upgrade and a websocket upgrade, with the 101 access-logged; no separate probe written.
This is skipped under -short. It re-runs itself in a child process with GODEBUG=http2xconnect=1 and checks the h2 echo. TestStreamDetachedHTTP11Upgrade covers the HTTP/1.1 upgrade in detached mode.
40 concurrent finish and markResult calls produce exactly one accounting of active, closed, duration and bytes. It exercises the stream type directly, not a real stream.
Table test with valid inputs and error cases; the adapt test checks the generated JSON. My probe parses uppercase WARN together with skip_handshake and stream_detached.
